input.question: Why do scars heal but leave a mark?
input.ground_truth: The skin you were born with took months to carefully grow in a controlled environment. When it gets badly damaged, your body doesn't have the time or conditions to replace it with identical tissue, so it rushes out a job to seal the wound, leaving out stuff like hair follicles and sweat glands to get the job done quicker.

Okay! Let’s imagine your skin is like a piece of paper.

When you get a cut or a scratch, it’s like tearing the paper a little bit. Your body sends in special helpers (like tiny workers) to fix the tear. These helpers patch up the paper so it doesn’t have a big hole anymore. That’s how the cut heals!

But, the way the helpers fix it isn’t exactly the same as the original paper. It’s a little bit different, kind of like if you put a sticker or a band-aid over the tear instead of making it exactly the same as before. That’s why you can see a mark or a line left behind — it’s the “band-aid” your body used to fix you up!

So, the cut gets better (heals), but the patch isn’t exactly the same, so you see a scar.
